questions.explanation: Array.from calls the mapper with a zero-based index, so the third element uses index two and equals 3895. The length sets how many values are produced. Both the direct number 3895 and the equivalent sum 1947 plus 1948 match, whereas 3893 and 3896 come from using the base value without the index and treating the index as one-based.
questions.hint: The mapper receives index values starting at zero.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — flat.
questions.explanation: flat with its default depth of one lifts the inner elements into a single array of length 2. The nested value 3894 becomes a normal element. The printed value is 2, while the alternatives come from counting only the outer subarrays, counting brackets as elements and adding one for nesting depth.
questions.hint: Default flat depth is one level.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — template length.
questions.explanation: The template literal expands to 'n=3895', which has 6 characters including the two-character prefix. Interpolation inserts the value as text. Carrying the operation through gives 6; common slips include ignoring the literal prefix and dropping a digit.
questions.hint: Count the literal characters around the interpolation.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving regex — test.

options.misconception: Assuming digits cannot match the pattern
Returning a descriptive word rather than a boolean

questions.explanation: test returns a boolean and the pattern finds at least one digit run in 'id=3896', so the result is true. The method does not return the matched text. The printed value is true, while the alternatives come from assuming digits cannot match the pattern, returning a descriptive word rather than a boolean and returning the matched substring.
questions.hint: test answers yes or no, not what matched.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — includes.

options.misconception: Assuming includes uses strict reference only for objects

questions.explanation: includes reports whether a value is present using same-value matching, so finding 3897 yields true. indexOf would return the position instead of a boolean. The printed value is true, while the alternatives come from assuming includes uses strict reference only for objects, returning the found element and returning an index-style position.
questions.hint: includes returns a boolean, not a position.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — length.
questions.explanation: push appends one element, so the list grows from 3 to 4 entries. The length property always counts elements, not the highest index. Carrying the operation through gives 4; common slips include counting before the push is applied and counting push as adding two slots.
questions.hint: push adds exactly one element to the end of an array.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — slice.

options.misconception: Assuming slice returns a copy of everything
Treating the slice end index as included
Treating the start index as the end

questions.explanation: slice takes elements from index 1 up to but not including index 3, which is two elements. The end boundary is exclusive, a common source of off-by-one confusion. The printed value is 2, while the alternatives come from treating the slice end index as included, treating the start index as the end and assuming slice returns a copy of everything.
questions.hint: The second argument of slice is not part of the result.
